senses.gloss: (v. קִשְׁקַשׁ I) to strike against; to touch closely.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 7:6">Bekh. VII, 6</cite> (<cite ref="Bekhorot 45a">45ᵃ</cite>) (expl. <he>עיקל</he>) <he>כל שמקיף … נוֹקְשׁוֹת וכ׳</he> (Mish. ed. <he>נושקות</he>) he whose legs do not touch each other when he puts his feet together.

senses.gloss: to cause striking against; to knock. Bekh. l. c. (44ᵇ) המַקִּישׁ בקרסוליו וכ׳ he who knocks his ankle-bones against each other (in walking, because his legs are bent outward), or rubs his legs against each other (his feet being bent outward). Midr. Sam. ch. IX מַקֶּשֶׁת ברגליה ומקשת בקרניה she knocks (creates a loud sound) with her feet and with her horns.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Zavim 4:1">Zab. IV, 1</cite>, sq. <he>ה׳ על וכ׳</he> if he knocked against &c.
Meg. 12ᵇ (play on בן קיש, Esth. II, 5) שה׳ על וכ׳ (Ms. M. שנָקַשׁ) he (Mordecai) knocked at the gates of mercy &c.; a. fr.—Esp. (cmp. נָגַן, נָכָה) to strike an instrument, play.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 18">Gen. R. s. 18</cite> (play on <he>הפעם</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 2:23">Gen. II, 23</cite>) <he>עתידה להַקִּישׁ עלי כזוג</he> (‘Rashi’: <he>לקשקש</he>) she is destined to be loud against me like a bell.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 31:1">Pesik. R. s. 31</cite>; <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 137:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. CXXXVII</cite> <he>אני מבקש שתעמדו ותַקִּישׁוּ</he> … <he>כדרך שהייתם מַקִּישִׁין וכ׳</he> I desire that you play on the cithern before me and the idol, as you played before your God.

Ib. אנו עומדים להַקִּישׁ וכ׳ shall we stand playing before this dwarf (Nebuchadnezzar) and this idol? Midr. Till. to Ps. XCII, end (play on יקשן, Gen. XXV, 2) שהיו מקישין בתוף לעכו״ם they struck the timbrel before idols; Yalk. Chr. 1073; Gen. R. s. 61 מקשין בית׳ (corr. acc.).—2) (cmp. נָקַף) to bring under the same category by juxtaposition, to compare.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 5a">Kidd. 5ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. (ref. to <he>ויצאה</he> a. <he>והיתה</he> in the same verse, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 24:2">Deut. XXIV, 2</cite>) <he>מקיש הויה ליציאה</he>, v. <cite ref="E00232"><he>הֲוָיָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Exodus 34:14">XXXIV, 14</cite>) <he>זביחה בכלל … להַקִּישׁ אליה</he> slaughtering for the idol would have been included in worshipping, and why is it singled out? To compare all other idolatrous functions with it: as slaughtering is a function performed inside &c.
<cite ref="Zevachim 5b:4">Zeb. 5ᵇ</cite> <he>הִקִּישׁוֹ הכתוב וכ׳</he> the text (<cite ref="Leviticus 7:37">Lev. VII, 37</cite>) places it side by side with peace offerings; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be placed side by side, to be compared.
units: <cite ref="Keritot 3a:52">Ker. 3ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 15:29">Num. XV, 29</cite>, sq.) <he>הוּקְּשָׁה כל התורה וכ׳</he> all the laws of the Torah are here placed on an equality with idolatry (as regards conditions of punishment). Ib. 2ᵇ <he>הוּקְּשׁוּ כל העריות כולן וכ׳</he> all laws concerning incest are put on an equality with &c. (<cite ref="Leviticus 18:29">Lev. XVIII, 29</cite>); a. fr.—Part. <cite ref="M00600"><he>מוּקָּשׁ</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 35">Gen. R. s. 35</cite> (play on <he>קשתי</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 9:13">Gen. IX, 13</cite>) <he>דבר שהוא מ׳ לי</he> something comparable with me (with the Divine Glory); Yalk. ib. 61; v. <cite ref="S01218"><he>קִישׁוּת</he> II</cite>.
